catalyst_text: NDA accepted priority review PDUFA set February 2027
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the NDA and granted Priority Review for an oral therapy targeting Stargardt Disease Type 1. The agency also assigned a PDUFA target action date of February 12, 2027, indicating an expedited review timeline for this indication.
catalyst_text_evidence: Belite Bio, Inc ... announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted and granted Priority Review designation of the New Drug Application (NDA) for tinlarebant for the treatment of Stargardt Disease Type 1 (STGD1). The FDA has set a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) date of 2027-02-12.

catalyst_text: Completed NDA submission acceptance and PDUFA date pending
detailed_catalyst_text: Completed the rolling New Drug Application submission to the FDA for treatment of Stargardt Disease Type 1. This milestone moves the program into the FDA’s 60-day acceptance review, after which a PDUFA action date may be assigned.
catalyst_text_evidence: Belite Bio, Inc (NASDAQ:BLTE) ("Belite Bio®" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage drug development company focused on advancing novel therapeutics targeting degenerative retinal diseases that have significant unmet medical needs, today announced the completion of its rolling submission of a New Drug Application (NDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for tinlarebant. The completed application will undergo the 60-day review period with the FDA, and if accepted, a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date will be assigned.

catalyst_text: Received Swiss orphan designation began FDA rolling NDA
detailed_catalyst_text: Swissmedic granted orphan drug status for this program in Stargardt disease. Positive pivotal Phase 3 results showed a 35.7% reduction in lesion growth, and a rolling NDA submission to the FDA has been initiated. These milestones underscore regulatory momentum and clinical validation in this rare disease.
catalyst_text_evidence: Belite Bio, Inc (NASDAQ:BLTE) ("Belite Bio®" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage drug development company focused on advancing novel therapeutics targeting degenerative retinal diseases that have significant unmet medical needs, today announced that the Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products (Swissmedic) has granted tinlarebant, the Company's lead product candidate, orphan drug status (ODS) for the treatment of Stargardt disease (STGD1), a rare, inherited retinal disorder caused by mutations in the ABCA4 gene. Company recently initiated a rolling submission of a New Drug Application (NDA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which it expects to complete in 2Q 2026. The trial met its primary efficacy endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 35.7% reduction in the growth rate of retinal lesions, measured as definitely decreased autofluorescence (DDAF) by fundus autofluorescence imaging, compared with placebo.

catalyst_text: Initiated rolling NDA submission under Breakthrough Therapy
detailed_catalyst_text: A rolling New Drug Application submission to the FDA was initiated for treatment of Stargardt Disease Type 1. This regulatory milestone, enabled by prior Breakthrough Therapy Designation and permission for rolling review, advances the program toward potential approval.
catalyst_text_evidence: Belite Bio, Inc (NASDAQ:BLTE) ("Belite Bio" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage drug development company focused on advancing novel therapeutics targeting degenerative retinal diseases that have significant unmet medical needs, today announced that it has initiated a rolling submission of an New Drug Application (NDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for tinlarebant, an investigational novel oral therapy for the treatment of Stargardt disease type 1 (STGD1), a rare, inherited retinal disorder caused by mutations in the ABCA4 gene. Tinlarebant has previously been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) by the FDA for STGD1, and the FDA has previously granted Belite approval for the rolling submission of the NDA.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 3 topline results meeting endpoint
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline results from the global Phase 3 DRAGON trial in adolescent Stargardt disease type 1 were reported. The study met the primary endpoint with a 36% reduction in retinal lesion growth versus placebo (p=0.0033) and showed supportive secondary outcomes with good tolerability. This is described as the first successful pivotal efficacy result in STGD1 and supports regulatory progress.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN DIEGO, 2025-12-01 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Belite Bio, Inc (NASDAQ:BLTE) ("Belite Bio" or the "Company") today announced topline results from the global Phase 3 "DRAGON" trial of Tinlarebant, marking the first successful pivotal trial in patients with Stargardt disease type 1 (STGD1). The Phase 3 DRAGON trial enrolled 104 patients with STGD1 and met its primary efficacy endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 36% reduction in the growth rate of retinal lesions, measured as definitely decreased autofluorescence (DDAF) by fundus autofluorescence imaging, compared with placebo. Statistical significance was reached when applying the pre-specified analysis (p-value = 0.0033). Tinlarebant was well tolerated throughout the trial.

catalyst_text: Interim Analysis Results for Ph3 Tinlarebant Trial
Data from the Phase 2/3 study over 24 months, presented at ARVO 2024, offered additional evidence for Tinlarebant's ability to slow down and possibly stop the progression of lesions, May 6, 2024.

The data from Phase 2, covering a 24-month period and presented at AAO, continues to highlight the safety profile of Tinlarebant and indicates a consistent reduction in DDAF lesion growth when compared to participants in the ProgStar study throughout the two-year treatment period.
Data from Phase 2 indicated that the treatment was safe and well tolerated in adolescents with Stargardt Disease (STGD1), as reported on April 25, 2023.
